games.description:
'2001', its add-a-ball version 'Dimension', and the add-a-ball export version 'Galaxie', all made by Gottlieb in 1971, are the first pinball machines to feature multiple banks of drop targets.

Maximum displayed point score is 9,999 points.

The game features a four flipper layout including numerous Lawlor staples, such as the shot through the bumpers, and the upper-flipper ramp shot. The game has many uniquely notable features including an animatronic hand with a built in magnet that will grab and lock pinballs for multiball, as well as a computer controlled mini flipper that, using artificial intelligence programming, learns to shoot a tricky cross-playfield shot with remarkable consistency. This game is also frequently credited with popularizing the "wizard mode" (despite not being the first game to have one). A true success for Bally/Williams, Addams Family holds an important place in pinball history, and well deserves its sought after status.
games.name: Addams Family, The

games.description: It's easy to see why Attack from Mars is one of the highest-rated pinball machines of all time. The game is a great shooter, making excellent use of the popular fan playfield layout with one of the best center playfield bash toys in the flying saucer, iconic callouts, and an approachable, easy-to-understand ruleset. Even today, it's a game that a lot of newer pins struggle to live up to. Blowing up a saucer (especially if you have a shaker motor attached) is always exciting.
games.name: Attack From Mars

games.description: Indiana Jones (not to be confused with the earlier Williams game Indiana Jones: The Pinball Adventure) is a pinball table made by Stern Pinball in 2008, coinciding with the release of Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull. It was designed by John Borg with artwork by Kevin O'Connor and programming by Keith Johnson. The game is all about the Indiana Jones film franchise, and there are four modes, one for each of them. It has a number of toys to further connect it to the movies, like recreations of the Ark, the Holy Grail, and the titular Crystal Skull, as well as a swordsman behind a wall. The game itself also has scenes from the movie fully recreated on the display. The game is also notable for having an eight-ball multiball mode, topped off with the infamous Ark scene from Raiders.
games.name: Indiana Jones

games.description: Indiana Jones: The Pinball Adventure is a popular game for many pinball collectors. It is a wide-body game, which means it is bigger than most other games. Among many other factors, people frequently like it because it doesn't suffer from some of the problems that other wide-body games have, like slow gameplay or shots that are difficult to make. There is a lot to do on the table, and the theme is well integrated with assets from all three of the original movies.
games.name: Indiana Jones - The Pinball Adventure

games.description:
Original table, designed in 2023. The table is based on the five indiana jones movies "Indiana jones The last Movie".

Indiana Jones The Last movie is made up of 12 missions and 3 super missions to activate the missions use the right ramp to enter the ark of the covenant which activates the missions. 4 successful missions trigger 1 super mission. 8 successful missions triggers the super missions 2 and 12 successful missions triggers the final mission The last movie. for the missions follow the instructions of the dmd.
find the 27 objects from the films by shooting the blue targets. The tilt has been deliberately lowered to be able to shake the ball on the top plate to shoot the captive ball more easily.
The Khazneh Petra monument activates several mystery, small dots, big dots, end of missions, extra ball, 2 ball etc. activating the lock ball 3 times triggers the multiball.

games.description: Lethal Weapon 3 is a pinball machine produced by Data East Pinball in 1992.It is based on the movie of the same name, which was the most popular film in summer 1992. The game featured a Generation 3 FullView dot matrix display, which was larger than the current industry standard, and displayed digitized movie clips.The game also featured a hidden leveling system, in which players "grab hold of the Data East gun handle and eliminate bad guys in one of three video crime simulator shoot outs".By 1994, it was Data East's all-time most successful pinball machine.The game was designed by Markus Rothkranz
games.name: Lethal Weapon 3

HAL 9000, the machine that murdered his crew, is back—and this time, he's inside a pinball machine. Relive the nightmare through brutal multi-balls and relentless boss fights.

Jack Bauer is back, but this time in Stern Pinball's new 24 pinball machine.

Stern Pinball takes FOX's hit television show and turns it into one fast-paced pinball machine that will excite both operators and homeowners.
250 cc is a pinball table with the theme of motorcycle sport, developed and published by the spanish INDER, which was released in Europe in 1992.

The flyer game may be a Sample game or an Early Production game.

It was designed as a retrofit for all electronic 4 player games except the wide body styled ones and included all the glass, decals and a new drop in playfield and sound and lamp modules.
games.name: 301 Bulls Eye

games.description:
4 Aces was produced by Williams Electronic in 1970.

Player presses button on lockdown bar to shoot ball into play from between the flippers. Pressing the flipper buttons triggers the upper flippers first then the lower ones. Ball hitting either of two hanging targets when lit for Bonus is stopped by an electromagnet and released after bonus points are scored.

Lighting the playing cards along the top of backglass awards Special and is a carry-over feature. Cabinet measures 24 1/4 inches wide.
games.name: 4 Aces

games.description:
Make a dated with 4 Queens.

Maximum displayed point score is 99,990 points.
games.name: 4 Queens

games.description:
Ladies of the rose themed game by Williams.

Features:
- Rotating targets turn and change from Red to Yellow alternately when hit. Five advances of either color increases the value of side holes from 50 to 100, to 200, to 300 and then to SPECIAL.
- Rotating targets turn when hit and when hole value is advanced. Rotating targets advance respective color 3 times when. "Triple Advance" is lit.
- Top rollover button lites two Jet Bumpers for 10 points, and Triple Advance, or SPECIAL on Rotating Targets.

Maximum displayed point score is 1,999 points.
games.name: 4 Roses

games.description: Your goal for this game is to complete sets of 1-2-3-4 numbered lanes and targets as many times as possible. There are five of each number on the playfield: one top lane, one side lane, one bottom return lane or out lane, one yellow target and one green target. Any of the five counts towards finishing a set of 1-2-3-4. Finishing a set scores 500 points and increases the value of one set of numbered lanes or targets from 50 to 200. The first set increases the top lanes; set #2 increases the yellow targets; set #3 increases the green targets. Completing a fourth set actually hurts your scoring opportunities, since the green targets now change to “special,” which is a free game in location play but worth nothing in tournament play. I wouldn't worry about it much, though, since to collect points, you need to keep scoring numbers. Just try to postpone finishing that fourth set and shoot all but one of the four numbers as much as you can.
games.name: 4 Square

games.description: Game is played in three "heats". Each heat puts three balls into play from the shooter lane automatically. A heat ends after all three balls drain. After three heats, the game ends.
games.name: 4x4 Atari

games.description:
On '8 Ball', the billiard balls have to be earned in numerical sequence so it made sense for this game to use for each player a sequential mechanism such as a stepper unit with reset coil. In contrast, because the billiard balls on 'Solids N Stripes' can be earned in any random order, it makes sense for that game to have relay banks which will track them in any order in which they are earned.

'8 Ball' is not the only Williams 2-player EM game that had playfield "memory" using alternating step-up units. An earlier game is Williams' 1956 'Piccadilly'. A subsequent game is Williams' 1968 'Pit Stop'.

On the backglass, the billiard players have cufflinks showing the initials "N.C." and "S.K.", a probable reference to Norm Clark and Steve Kordek. Cufflinks with identical initials are also found on the backglasses of Williams' 1971 'Planets' and Williams' 1971 'Zodiac'.
games.name: 8 Ball

games.description: A Charlie Brown Christmas feat. The Vince Guaraldi Trio — A cozy, holiday-themed VPX table inspired by the 1965 Peanuts special. Featuring Vince Guaraldi's classic jazz soundtrack, charming visuals, and immersive gameplay with optional VR support.

games.description: Aaron Spelling (1923-2006) was an American television and film producer. Data East was commissioned by his second wife to build this game, as her gift to him. The company modified a game that was currently being made, Data East's 1992 'Lethal Weapon 3'.

games.description:
With its mysterious magic and sorcery theme and unique layout, Abra Ca Dabra is one of the most beloved games released by Gottlieb in the mid-1970s. 

The game features a moving lit drop target that will score an indicated bonus value, a value which is increased by completing the rollover sequence or hitting the centre target after collecting all the drop targets. The same layout appeared in Gottlieb's soccer themed games Team One and Kicker.
games.name: Abra Ca Dabra

Available with english or german lettering.

There also exists an identical model where just the name has been changed to ACES TOP.

Navigate stormy waters, dock at mysterious islands, and face legendary sea creatures as you chart your course toward hidden treasure. With shifting tides, dynamic playfield features, and immersive nautical soundscapes, Adventure delivers a true sailor's journey, full of risk, reward, and endless replayability.

Design supremacy blending the best of player grabbing graphics and play action to generate highest possible machine profits.

Players will delight as they join famous Agents 777 (Elliot Nest, Melvin Nervous & J. Edgar Snooper) in a flipper game experience.

Lightning fast play action, maximum ball control, multitude of skill shots and slot machine playfield area awards arrests player interest for repeated play and profits....up to 10X regular multipliers plus 2X-3X-4X Super Bonus Multiplier. Exciting audio, get-a-away car, sirens, gun fire, jack pot bell, all features to make Agents 777 a sure shot winner.

games.description: Beauty of an art piece, but a dog of a game. All pinball is good pinball, but this just isn't a very good game. Little flow from the King of Flow Steve Ritchie's first offering before he hit his stride with Williams. A big clunky widebody that doesn't use any of its space very well.
games.name: Airborne Avenger

games.description:
Airport by Gottlieb is the first game with vari-targets. It also has a ball return feature that has no limit on the times it can be used. Interestingly there is no special or bonus on this game. This pinball requires more nudging and bumping to keep the ball in play than most games.

Airport also made in a 4-player version Gottlieb's 1969 'College Queens' but with different artwork.
games.name: Airport

games.description:
Al Capone is a clone of Bally's Speakeasy but without the mechanical Roulette Wheel. The remaining rules are quite similiar with subtle changes.

Two funny facts about the Sacrifice Button:
- You have the option to reset top cards out of order even after the last ball. This will do no good but will cost You 25.000 points anyway.
- If You have lit cards "5" to "8" out of order, You can use the Sacrifice Button to relight the "Sequence" light without resetting any card.
games.name: Al Capone

games.id: Al's Garage Band Goes On A World Tour (AlvinG 1992)(2.5.2)
games.description:
Al's Garage Band was based on people known by the conceptor : Al, Gloria, Delmore, and Dr. Skins. Only one character, Stitchy, was not a real person.

The game in the manufacturer's flyer shows a VUK (A device that kicks the ball straight up, usually onto a habitrail.) at the end of the horseshoe ramp in middle right playfield at what would be the "top lock". This VUK was subsequently removed by the manufacturer. Reportedly, twenty games were made with this top lock VUK.

games.description: Algar is not a favorite, but still gets used. The highest-value shots on it are for the three captive balls on the right, but the playfield layout makes those high-risk. There's a drain channel right of the right slingshot and it's a common misery to go one captive ball shot and out there. The problem is, the other shots on the game don't add value that quickly and aren't terribly safe, either; Algar is lots of grinding and trying to survive random bounces.
games.name: Algar

games.description:
Ali is a Licensed Pinball Table that pays tribute to the legendary boxer Muhammad Ali. It was designed by famed pinball designer Harry Williams and released in 1980 by Stern Electronics. Like Muhammad Ali himself, this is a fast, bombastic game that never lets players forget who they're up against.

The table is festooned with famous Ali-isms, such as "I am the Greatest", "Three-Time Champ", "Ali Shuffle" and "Rope-A-Dope", all drawn with comic-style pop lettering. The center of the playfield has a portrait of Ali pointing at the player along with a facsimile of his signature, while the backglass features the boxer's face surrounded by his form in the ring. The game also supported the then-new Susan B. Anthony dollar coin, and gave players an extra game for using one.
games.name: Ali

games.description: This multiball game has some crazy fantasy alien gambling artwork. The 5 Bank Drop targets right in the middle of the playfield are the major targets for this game. You need to hit them in order to maximize the Royal Flush Value. You can also hit the 4 kings across the top of the playfield to multiply the royal flush value. There are other things to shoot for but the center drops with the top lane multipliers are you main shots. This particular machine is a beautiful example of this game.
games.name: Alien Poker

games.description: Alien Star is a pinball machine from June 1984, manufactured by D. Gottlieb & Co. Journey to an Alien Star, for a pinball battle in space. Multiball, skill shots and plenty of fast action bring this fantasy world alive for your players.
games.name: Alien Star

games.description: This Game was made while Elvis was still alive and Brunswick couldn't get the rights to call it Elvis so they used an image of a Elvis look alike with a Afro which Tom Jones wore at the time. Both Artists were popular at the time.

games.description: This game apparently was advertised only as 'bowling' (while the German sign on the playfield, "alle neune", was secondary. An USA version have been see with an English playfield sign indicating "big strike". On these games, a round sticker is covering the beer steins on the lower left playfield and may be intended to be a bowling ball. The words "BOWLING big strike" appear on this sticker.
games.name: Alle Neune

games.description: Aloha is one of several Polynesian-themed games from the early 1960s including Paradise and Tropic Isle. This machine, in particular, has both a beautiful playfield and backglass with multiple lovely hula dancers in bright purple, yellow, and red colors.nnnnAlthough the concept of play is simple, build up yellow and red bonus points and collect, it can be very difficult to actually collect the point you build up, especially in a two-player game. That's because the bonus will carry over to each player and ever the next game! In addition to the tricky flipper gap, there is also a large gobble hole which can be both an asset and a setback depending on if it is lit or if there are bonus points stored up. Overall, this is a great example of an early 60s pin with all the bells and lights you need.
games.name: Aloha

games.description: The Amazing Spiderman is a wide-body pinball, release in 1980 by Gottlieb. Based on the Marvel character it features character poses taken directly from Marvel comics and style guides including Aunt May, Kingpin, Lizard, Scorpion, Vulture, Black Widow, Kraven the Hunter and the Green Goblin. It was the first of Gottlieb's System 80 design pinball machines. It also was the first Gottlieb pinball, with an "attract mode" lighting. In which various playfield lights, alternate between off an on. It was also the first solid state pinball with the speaker in the backbox instead of the bottom cabinet.
games.name: Amazing Spider-man, The

games.description: Amazon is a jungle-themed pinball adventure set in the heart of the Amazon, featuring wild targets, vibrant artwork, and classic 1970s gameplay.

AMERICA 1492 a pin-ball designed with all the details, for a new generation.
- 4 players with 7 digits.
- Regulations of Extra Ball and plays/Games.
games.name: America 1492

games.description:
Amigo is the first game that legend Greg Kmiec designed before creating such classics as Xenon, Captain Fantastic, Pinball Wizard, Six Million Dollar Man, and more. In fact there are several elements of this game in common with Six Million Dollar Man as game features PlayMore Post between the flippers, spinner, side gate. A fantastic first game for Greg but must have been made before his Single Red Post signature that he developed later on to spite Bally who didn't allow designers to have their name on their designs at the time.
The game in the flyer has the so-called "inverted backbox" where the front frame is wider at the bottom than at the top, as if "upside-down" from typical Bally backboxes, leaving a small ledge at the base of the backglass.nnnnThis backbox showed up again on a test game for Bally's 1976 'Flip Flop'.
games.name: Amigo

games.description: Playmatic produced this game twice as evidenced by the two sets of flyers, the second time with simplified playfield artwork and new melodies. The backglasses in the flyers are slightly different as well. nnnnTheme :	Dragons, Fantasy
games.name: Antar

games.description: Apache is an electro-mechanical table channeling a gritty underworld vibe (the term “apache” referred to Parisian gangsters), it features classic EM design with two flippers, pop bumpers, and mechanical scoring reels. Digitally recreated in VPX with authentic artwork restoration and optional VR/backglass support.
games.name: Apache

games.description: Brazilian machine from 1978 based on Gottlieb's FAST DRAW
games.name: Apache!

games.description: The Apollo and Blast Off pinball machines were both manufactured by Williams in 1967 as part of their effort to capitalize on the excitement surrounding the NASA space program.  These electro-mechanical machines feature space exploration themes. Apollo was the replay version, while Blast Off was the add-a-ball version.
games.name: Apollo

games.description: Apollo 13 is a 1995 pinball game by Sega Pinball, based on the film of the same name. Kevin Bacon (Jack Swigert), Bill Paxton (Fred Haise), and Gary Sinise (Ken Mattingly) provided custom speech for this game. This is a very dense pinball table; playfield toys include an elevating Saturn V rocket, a lunar LEM module, a countdown LED, and a rotating Moon.nnnnCollect orbits around the table to Advance the Spacecraft around the Moon and return to Earth, and perform various Apollo Missions along the way perform a manual burn to straighten the orbiter, fix the Life Support systems, fix the CO2 scrubbers, and take care of the Master Alarm.nnnnFor more points, shoot the Saturn and load up for multiball, or use gravitynote to slingshot pinballs over the Moon.nnnnEven with all these features, the biggest appeal of the game is its 13 Ball Blastoff Multiball, where thirteen balls are unloaded onto the playfield. Up to six people can play at once, either individually or in teams, and the game offers "Novice" and "Wizard" difficulty settings for players.
games.name: Apollo 13

games.description: Manufacturer: Juegos Populares, S.A., of Madrid, Spain (1986)nnType: Solid State Electronic (SS)nnTheme: Amusement Park - WaternnNotable Features:nnFlippers (2), Pop bumpers (2), Slingshots (2), 3-bank drop targets (1), Standup target (1), Vari-target (1), Kick-out hole (1), Rollunder spinner (1). The left outlane has a gate that, when activated, changes the outlane into an inlane, returning the ball to the flipper.
games.name: Aqualand

games.description: Aquarius marks an important milestone in pinball history as Gottlieb's first machine to use a chime box. This distinctive feature remained a hallmark in all their machines until 1978 when it was eventually replaced with a soundboard. The chime box in Aquarius adds a unique auditory dimension to your gaming experience, invoking a sense of nostalgia that only classic pinball can deliver.
games.name: Aquarius

games.description:
﻿Enter the Exciting World of ARENA. Gottlieb's Newest Hit by Premier Technology® combines the Challenge of Battle with the Power and Speed of Pinball.
- Using the Plunger as a "Skill Shot" propel yourself into the PIT area to score SPECIAL, EXTRA-BALL, 1 MILLION points, or RAMP VALUE. Now you enter the Main ARENA playfield.
- Shoot through the Spinner to complete the L-O-K Lanes. Lock 1 Ball, then 2 Balls and finally RELEASE for 3 Ball Action.
- Knock down the "WALL" targets and with only seconds to spare, Battle with the "GUARD" to light up EXTRA BALL in the PIT.
- Shoot the RAMP to increase RAMP VALUE. The RAMP opens the GATE to either "Return to Flipper" or "Back to the Plunger" to face the PIT.
- Making P-I-T Lanes lights I MILLION in the PIT.
- C-Y-S Targets Increase MULTIPLIER and lights SPECIAL.
games.name: Arena

games.description: 1977 William's Argosy 4 player ultra fast playing pinball machine with all the features you could want in a 1970's pinball machine. Historically significant Argosy was the last 4 player machine made by William's. It was one of the last machines ever made before the pinball industry went digital and the world lost something special the sounds and feel of a electro-mechanical pinball machine.
games.name: Argosy

games.description: This is a 1979 Williams/United Aristocrat shuffle alley bowler. Up to six players. After feeding the coins, you press start the number of times for each player, then you can press the select button to pick the game mode you want. This is an older bowler with electronic sounds.
games.name: Aristocrat

games.description:
This is Arizona by LTD do Brasil in 1977.
 
The table has no DIP switch menu to adjust the number of balls or other settings. At the end of a game there is a match feature that awards a credit for scores ending on 50 or 70, depending on the number shown in the "Ball in Play" display.
games.name: Arizona

games.description: The theme of the machine is skiing. There were two versions of Aspen made. The first version is Model 558602002 and uses a 3 bar chimebox for sounds. The gameboard is wired differently than the later version and does NOT interchange with it. This version was made around October 1977. The second version is Model 558602282 and uses electronic sounds and has a speaker. This version came out in late October 1978 and is wired the same as the Alive game.
games.name: Aspen

games.description: This is a re-theme of jpsalas's "Serious Sam II" table.
games.name: Asterix the Twelve Tasks

games.description:
Asteroid Annie and the Aliens is a 1980 Gottlieb arcade pinball game. The game is as straightforward as the name — Token Human Annie is playing poker against her alien companions, and she needs your help to assemble a winning hand.

Use the rollovers to select a suit, then hit the various drop targets to collect tens, Jacks, Queens, Kings, and Aces. Collect extra balls along the way so Annie can keep taking her martian marks to the cleaners.
games.name: Asteroid Annie and the Aliens

games.description:
Original table, designed in 2016

This table includes sounds from original asteroids game. Also has rotating asteroid, and lighting. Scoring issue where score jumps up then back down. Middle island needed adjustment for shooting.
games.name: Asteroids

games.description: Astro the italian version from Gottieb of Star trek. The replay version of this game is Gottlieb's 1971 '4 Square' but with different artwork.
games.name: Astro
