New Memory Super Bonus Once a 20,000 bonus score is achieved, 20,000 points are recalled and added with every ball.
games.name: Playboy

games.description:
The "Playboy 35th Anniversary" pinball machine, commemorates the 35th anniversary of Playboy magazine with a theme centered around a poolside party at Hugh Hefner's Playboy mansion. This solid-state machine features two flippers, three pop bumpers, and two ramps, alongside a 3-ball multiball mode.

This game was produced from May 1989 to August 1989.
games.name: Playboy 35th Anniversary

games.description:
The "Playboy 35th Anniversary" pinball machine, commemorates the 35th anniversary of Playboy magazine with a theme centered around a poolside party at Hugh Hefner's Playboy mansion. This solid-state machine features two flippers, three pop bumpers, and two ramps, alongside a 3-ball multiball mode.

This game was produced from May 1989 to August 1989.
games.name: Playboy 35th Anniversary

games.description:
Domino and PlayMates, both are electro-mechanical pinball machines. Domino is the replay version, while PlayMates is the add-a-ball variant.

Maximum displayed point score is 9,999 points.
games.name: Playmates

games.description: Original table, designed in 2016 by JPSALAS. The goal of the game is to achieve the highest score by catching Pokémon, hatching eggs and catching Pokémon give the highest scores (and bonus). You'll get plenty of extra modes, with multiballs, combos, jackpots, and coins to upgrade your ball.
games.name: Pokemon Pinball

games.description: Pokemon Slots is an original, fan-made virtual slots-themed table inspired by the Celadon City game corner from the Pokémon games on GameBoy Color. It recreates the nostalgic slot machine experience, allowing players to earn credits by spinning one to three lines and manually stopping each reel. The gameplay is simple yet engaging—players select lines with the right flipper, confirm with the left, and then spin and stop the reels to try their luck. Featuring themed artwork and a complete backglass, the table delivers a fun and nostalgic twist on classic arcade gameplay, with future updates teased to include prizes and 3D visuals.
games.name: Pokemon Slots

games.description: Pokerino is a solid-state pinball machine features a poker and casino theme. This game has Double Action Flippers which allows the inner flippers to operate first, or all four flippers to operate, depending on how far the flipper buttons are pressed.
games.name: Pokerino

games.description: Polar Explorer is a solid-state pinball machine designed for up to four players. The game features an arctic exploration theme, challenging players to navigate treacherous ice and snow. Its playfield design is similar to Zaccaria's "Pinball Champ" from the same year.
games.name: Polar Explorer

games.description: Pole Position is a solid state pinball table. It is unrelated to the popular arcade Namco game of the same name.
games.name: Pole Position

games.description: Original table, designed in 2019. It is based on Jpsalas's tables "Miraculous". This table is a tribute to Police Academy, a comedy franchise of seven theatrical films and two spin-off television shows.
games.name: Police Academy

games.description: The "Police Force" pinball machine is a unique game featuring anthropomorphic jungle animals as police officers and criminals. The objective is to arrest four key criminals: a loan shark, a machine gun-toting crocodile, a diamond thief weasel, and a drug-dealing rat, ultimately allowing players to score a progressive jackpot.
games.name: Police Force

games.description:
Polo and Mini Cycle both games share the same playfield design, with Polo being the four-player version and Mini Cycle the two-player variant. These machines feature two flippers, three pop bumpers, a vari-target, a kick-out hole, and a free ball return lane.

The playfield layout was used again on Gottlieb's 1972 'Space Orbit' made for export to Italy.
games.name: Polo

games.description: Original table, designed in 2022. It is based on Jpsalas's table "Wrath of the Olympus" and inspired by the Poltergeist movies from the 80's, especially the first and the second.
games.name: Poltergeist

games.description:
- Trumpet the open and close of the game, Siren for super scoring hit, and Raspberry for a miss.
- New ADVANCE feature and lure of "soaring-scoring power", to shoot for a top 1260 points! ADVANCE increases scoring values for spares and strikes by 20 or 30-points as play advances!
- Flashing Red lights can launch a storm of super scoring for players on a hot roll!
games.name: Pompeii

games.description: This solid-state table features a billiards theme and includes two flippers, three pop bumpers, multiple drop targets, and a unique 8-ball or 9-ball game option.
games.name: Pool Sharks

games.description: "Drop-A-Card" and "Pop-A-Card" are two electro-mechanical pinball released in the early 1970s. "Drop-A-Card" (1971) is a replay version where players can earn free games by scoring points, while "Pop-A-Card" (1972) is an add-a-ball version focused on awarding extra balls. Both games feature card-themed layouts and include various drop targets, pop bumpers, and star rollovers.
games.name: Pop A Card

games.description:
Released under the Bally name, Popeye Saves the Earth was the last of the highly successful WPC DSD Superpin line of games produced by WMS Inc. from 1993 to 1994. It was also was Python Anghelo's last mass produced pinball machine.

Released in February 1994, and co-designed with Barry Oursler, Popey managed to sell 4,217 units.

Popeye's theme is primarily based upon the 125 classic Popeye the Sailor animated shorts made between 1933 to 1957 by Fleischer Studios/Paramount Famous Studios, which Python was a huge fan of.

Some machines received a large 3D Bluto head in the center of the playfield, which was replaced with a smaller flat version, due to early complaints. Reproductions and original Bluto heads are highly sought after by owners today.
games.name: Popeye Saves the Earth

games.description: This game is the version of Gottlieb's 1978 'Neptune' made for export to Italy. The replay version of this game is Gottlieb's 1978 'Hit the Deck'.
games.name: Poseidon

games.description: Primordial Quarry is an original sci-fi pinball adventure set on a mysterious alien mining planet. Dig deep through hazardous tasks, extract exotic minerals, and uncover ancient secrets hidden beneath the surface. Fast, dynamic gameplay with unique modes and challenges await!
games.name: Primordial Quarry

games.description:
Each of the four players uses the same four electro-mechanical score reels. Each of the top four lanes lights a pop bumper. The apron has a small LCD used in attract mode to display the replay value to beat.

Maximum displayed point score is 9,999 points.
games.name: Primus

games.description: Original table, designed in 2023. This game is inspired by The Princess Bride, a 1987 American fantasy adventure comedy film directed and co-produced by Rob Reiner.
games.name: Princess Bride

games.description: Original table designed in 2018, this is a tribute to Prison Break, an 2005's American crime drama television series created by Paul Scheuring for Fox. The series revolves around two brothers: Lincoln Burrows (Dominic Purcell) and Michael Scofield (Wentworth Miller).
games.name: Prison Break

games.description:
An electro-mechanical game features a billiards theme, challenging players with two sets of seven drop targets that represent the solids and stripes in pool, along with a critical eight ball target. This game was exported to Italy as Gottlieb's 1972 'Play Pool'.

The replay versions of this game are the 2-player Gottlieb's 1974 'Big Shot' and the 4-player Gottlieb's 1973 'Hot Shot'.
games.name: Pro Pool

games.description:
Designed by Ed Krynski with art by Gordon Morison, Pro-Football has a different plunger. It does not shoot up the side, it is launched by a coil right between the flippers in the center of the field and is angled to shoot slightly to the right side. The 2-player version is Gottlieb's 1977 'Gridiron' but with different artwork.
As far as the gameplay goes, the yellow side targets add 1 point to the point score. Advancing 100 yards scores a touchdown which adds 6 to the point score and 6000 to the high score. Football resets to start position when a touchdown is made.
games.name: Pro-Football

games.description: An electro-mechanical machine featuring a western theme inspired by prospecting for gold. The game's backglass notably features a comedic depiction of prospectors, which some sources suggest is based on the Laurel and Hardy film Way Out West.
games.name: Prospector

games.description: Single player Italian version of 2-player Gottlieb's 1970 'Crescendo' and 4-player Gottlieb's 1970 'Groovy'.
games.name: Psychedelic

games.description: Punk! has a music theme and includes four flippers, no ramps, and a three-ball multiball mode.
games.name: Punk

games.description:
The Pyramid is notable for being the first Gottlieb's solid-state pinball machine. this table features a historical Egyptian theme. The playfield includes two flippers, three pop bumpers, three standup targets, and a five-bank drop target, providing varied gameplay.

The 4-player EM version of this game is Gottlieb's 1977 'Cleopatra'. The 4-player SS version is Gottlieb's 1977 'Cleopatra'.
games.name: Pyramid

games.description: Q*Bert's Quest is a pinball machine features a video game theme inspired by the classic arcade game Q*Bert, with four flippers, no ramps, and no multiball mode. It was part of the Gottlieb System 80A series, with a total production of 884 units.
games.name: Q-Bert's Quest

games.description:
Original table, designed in 2021. This is a tribute to the Singer The Queen.

There are 2 tables : 
 - Queen - The Game Hits 1
 - Queen - The Game Hits 2

The main distinctions between these tables are the playfield and music.
games.name: Queen - The Game Hits

games.description:
Original table, designed in 2021. This is a tribute to the Singer The Queen.

There are 2 tables : 
 - Queen - The Game Hits 1
 - Queen - The Game Hits 2

The main distinctions between these tables are the playfield and music.
games.name: Queen - The Game Hits

games.description: Queen of Hearts is a single-player electro-mechanical pinball machine, the game features two flippers, three pop bumpers, two passive bumpers, two slingshots, and five gobble holes.
games.name: Queen of Hearts

games.description:
This table features a Western theme and includes two flippers, three pop bumpers, two 5-bank drop targets with trip arms, four standup targets, and two kick-out holes.

The 4-player version of this game is Gottlieb's 1975 'Fast Draw'.
games.name: Quick Draw

games.description: The Quicksilver pinball machine is celebrated for its fast-paced gameplay and distinctive sci-fi theme. the table features a sleek playfield layout with dual spinners, numerous drop targets, and three pop bumpers, offering players a variety of challenging shots.
games.name: Quicksilver

games.description: This pinball machine was the last production made by Juegos Populares before the factory was closed down.
games.name: Quijote

games.description: "Rack 'Em Up" has a pool and billiards theme, featuring two flippers, no ramps, and no multiball. It is part of the Gottlieb System 80A series. A total of 1,762 units were produced.
games.name: Rack Em Up

games.description: The Rack-A-Ball pinball machine features a billiards theme and is part of the electro-mechanical (EM) era, the game is notable for its distinctive mechanical backbox animation, which simulates pool balls lining up as the game progresses.nnnnSame playfield layout as Gottlieb's 1964 'Bowling Queen' and Gottlieb's 1969 'Mibs'.
games.name: Rack-A-Ball

games.description: A pinball machine inspired by late 80s / early 90s skater culture with a wide variety of shots and a "mega-million" feature that can award anywhere from 3 to 10 million points.
games.name: Radical

games.description: Rails is an original Visual Pinball X table inspired by classic electro-mechanical machines, featuring a charming train theme. The gameplay revolves around completing color patterns, hitting drop targets, and activating rollover switches to unlock “Train Mode,” a high-scoring phase with dynamic elements. With its nostalgic look, clever layout, and satisfying challenges, Rails offers a perfect mix of vintage style and modern gameplay depth.
games.name: Rails

games.description: The "Rainbow" pinball machine is a single-player, electro-mechanical game. The backglass carries Gottlieb's famous phrase: Amusement Pinballs, as American as Baseball and Hot Dogs!
games.name: Rainbow

games.description: Original table, designed in 2021.  It is based on "Raven" from Gottlieb in 1986 and inspired by Rambo, an American media franchise centered on a series of action films. The five movies are First Blood (1982), Rambo: First Blood Part II (1985), Rambo III (1988), Rambo (2008), and Rambo: Last Blood (2019). Its titular protagonist is a United States Army Special Forces veteran played by Sylvester Stallone.
games.name: Rambo

games.description: Rancho is a classic electro-mechanical pinball machines share a Western theme and feature the same gameplay mechanics, including a unique animated backbox where a horse kicks a cowboy.nnnnSame playfield like Buckaroo the replay version and Cow Poke the add-a-ball variant.
games.name: Rancho

games.description: Rapid Fire was Bally's response to Williams' 1981 'Hyperball'. The pre-production working name of this game was 'Cross Fire' as evidenced in Bally's "Numerical List of Machines".
games.name: Rapid Fire

games.description: This table features a military theme and inculde two flippers, one ramp, and an alphanumeric display. The game is noted for its unique backglass art, depicting a female soldier.nnnnThis machine was the first pinball machine from any manufacturer to use a photograph for a backglass or translite.
games.name: Raven

games.description: Stern acquired Chicago Coin Machine Company in December 1976 and 'Rawhide' was its first 4-player game, a continuation of the production of Chicago Coin's 1977 'Rawhide'.nnnnThe 2-player version of this game is Stern's 1977 'Stampede'.
games.name: Rawhide

games.description: Raygun Runner is an original cyberpunk style Visual Pinball table where you play a rogue smuggler in a dystopian future. Navigate through missions to collect parts, craft rayguns, and deliver them while evading drones, aliens, and corporate enforcers. Unlock badges like Scavenger or Gun Slinger, trigger multiball modes, and build up to a final showdown. With dynamic ramps, layered objectives, and immersive visuals, Raygun Runner delivers a fast-paced, story-driven pinball experience.
games.name: Raygun Runner

games.description: "Ready… Aim… Fire!," is a solid-state pinball machine with a military target-shooting theme. It features two flippers and no multiball, focusing instead on strategic shots to advance through the game. The machine uses the Gottlieb System 80A hardware, and 2,436 units were produced.
games.name: Ready...aim...fire!

games.description:
The primary goal is to help Red and Ted, a pair of road construction workers, travel through the United States from east to west. The player can visit a total of 18 different cities/states, each of which starts its own scoring mode.The game features a "wizard mode" called Super Payday, which can be started by visiting any of the last three cities in the above list and locking two balls as indicated on the display and playfield before the mode timer runs out.
Up to five extra balls can be earned per play; a score award is given for each one earned thereafter.
games.name: Red And Ted's Road Show

games.description: Red Baron and Blue Max two related pinball machines produced by Chicago Coin in 1975. Blue Max is the four-player version, while Red Baron is its two-player counterpart. Both games share the same playfield layout but differ in artwork. These machines featured two flippers, two pop bumpers, two slingshots, two spinning targets, and two drop targets.
games.name: Red Baron

games.description: Remdwaas Pokémon Pinball is an original Visual Pinball X table developed by Remdwaas, inspired by the classic Pokémon Pinball games from the Game Boy era. Centered around the first 151 Pokémon, it blends elements from Red/Blue and Ruby/Sapphire into a nostalgic and dynamic pinball adventure. You play as Ash, beginning in Pallet Town, catching and evolving Pokémon, battling trainers, and earning gym badges. Instead of multiballs, Pikachu serves as a ball saver, and various modes and mini-games faithfully capture the spirit of the original handheld titles. A fast-paced, retro-styled table crafted with creativity and care.
games.name: Remdwaas Pokemon Pinball

games.description: "Rescue 911," is based on the TV show of the same name. It features three flippers, two ramps, and a three-ball multiball mode. The game includes a helicopter toy that picks up the ball, adding a unique interactive element. It captures the essence of emergency rescue missions.
games.name: Rescue 911

games.description: Original table, designed in 2016 and themed about zombie.
games.name: Retro Zombie Adventure Land

games.description:
A modified copy of Gottlieb's 1967 'King of Diamonds'. The result made for a faster game, one preferred and considered better by Spanish pinball players. The game was a sensation and so successful that Petaco sold hundreds of them, many to replace ones that had worn out in only three months of use. Surprised Gottlieb personnel traveled to Spain because they could not understand the success.

'Rey de Diamantes' means 'King of Diamonds'.
games.name: Rey de Diamantes

games.description: Rider's Surf is a solid-state pinball machine features a surfing theme, incorporating two flippers and two pop bumpers. As a product of a relatively obscure manufacturer, "Rider's Surf" is considered rare, with limited production and distribution, making it a unique find among pinball enthusiasts and collectors.
games.name: Rider's Surf

games.description:
Object: Join Robert Ripley on his quest to visit the seven continents of the world and collect strange objects.
Visit continents: Shoot the ball into the variable push target to visit continents. Watch the display for instructions on collecting items.
Temple code: Shoot the ball into the temple (center ramp) to turn on lights in the Tic-Tac-Toe panel on the playfield. Completing any 3 in a row will give you the indicated reward.
Jackpots: While in multiball, shoot for the ramps and the side loop shot.
Super jackpot: After 2 jackpots are collected, super jackpot will light on the upper side shot.
Ripleys letters: Collect R-I-P-L-E-Y-S letters by collecting objects while visiting continents.
Hint: Collect all 7 R-I-P-L-E-Y-S letters to visit the mystery 8th continent!
games.name: Ripleys Believe It Or Not

games.description: Riverboat Gambler is a gambling-themed pinball machine featuring a unique blend of pinball and casino games, the machine incorporates elements like a roulette wheel and various card games into its gameplay. It has two flippers, three pop bumpers, and multiple drop targets. Players can place bets on a virtual roulette wheel integrated into the backglass, enhancing the game's casino ambiance.
games.name: Riverboat Gambler

games.description: "Road Race" and "Stock Car" are two pinball machines produced by Gottlieb in the 1960s, both themed around auto racing. "Road Race" is the replay version, while "Stock Car" is the add-a-ball version, which was a popular feature in regions where awarding replays was not allowed. These machines are characterized by their vibrant racing-themed artwork and straightforward gameplay that emphasizes skill shots, making them favorites among both casual players and collectors.
games.name: Road Race

games.description: Road Runner is a widebody pinball machine themed after the popular Looney Tunes cartoon character. Road Runner was designed by Marty Rosenthal.
games.name: Road Runner

games.description: Robo-War features a sci-fi robot theme with two flippers, one ramp, and a two-ball multiball mode. Part of the Gottlieb System 80B series. A total of 2,130 units were produced.
games.name: Robo-War

games.description:
Robocop is a tie-in to the 1987 smash movie featuring the titular cyborg super-cop. As RoboCop, the player must patrol the streets of Detroit, enforcing his Prime Directives while arresting lawbreakers of all types. Capture Emil Antonowsky, Clarence Boddicker, and Dick Jones, then jump the Entry Ramp to start multiball. Spell ROBOCOP for random rewards and an extra ball, then get some target practice and confront ED-209 for a million-point bonus, all while the game plays memorable quotes from the film.
Among pinball die-hards, RoboCop is considered a mediocre table, with lackluster artwork and a shallow ruleset; it's possible to rack up a high score at the game simply by repeatedly shooting the Entry Ramp jump and left spinner orbit. None of this matters one iota to the game's fans, who find it fast and fun, a back-to-basics game with great music and a memorable light show that provides a simple way to revisit the iconic movie.
games.name: Robocop

games.description: Original table, designed in 2018 and inspired by the movie of the same name.
games.name: Robocop 3
Robot

games.description: Robot Invasion is an original Visual Pinball X table set in a sci-fi universe where players battle waves of hostile robots. With fast-paced gameplay, intense multiball sequences, and dynamic lighting effects, the table delivers a high-energy pinball experience full of action and chaos.
games.name: Robot Invasion

games.description: The "Rock" pinball machine features a distinctive music theme, capitalizing on the rock 'n' roll culture of the era. This table inculde mini-playfield at upper left.
games.name: Rock

games.description: Playmatic's Rock 2500 (1985) and Black Fever (1980) are solid-state pinball machines sharing identical playfield layouts but featuring distinct artwork.
games.name: Rock 2500

games.description: The Rock Star (1978) and Blue Note (1979) are nearly identical but differ slightly in gameplay focus and scoring. Rock Star is an add-a-ball machine, primarily marketed for export to Italy (The last export), while Blue Note is a replay version designed for domestic markets.
games.name: Rock Star

games.description: The manufacturer produced the backglasses in both crystal glass and Plexiglas.
games.name: Rocket III

games.description: The RockMakers pinball machine features a prehistoric theme with dinosaurs and T-Rex imagery. An arc of mini-rollover buttons in lower playfield spells out R-O-C-K M-A-K-E-R-S. A ball having perfect trajectory can score the entire arc. Each player has a Rock-A-Rock score reel on the backglass to count the number of times either R-O-C-K or M-A-K-E-R-S is achieved. A Rock-A-Rock threshold can be set to award extra ball or replay
games.name: Rockmakers

games.description:
Rocky is a Pinball Table designed by John Trudeau with art by David Moore. It was an indirect tie-in to Rocky III, and was released by Gottlieb in 1982.
Not surprisingly, the Rocky pinball pits the player in a ten-round boxing match; knock down the drop target corresponding to the current round to advance to the next. More surprisingly is the unconventional table layout, which has two pairs of flippers at the bottom of the playfield. Extra balls and specials are available for going through seven or more rounds, and an "Instant Win" button gives beginners a fighting chance. Cheering crowds and the "Rocky" theme music round out the package.
Sharp-eyed filmgoers will notice that the Rocky pinball machine is not the one that appears in Rocky III; that was a prop backglass installed on an existing pinball table. Only three of the prop backglasses were made. One was destroyed on-camera, and the surviving two are in possession of private collectors.
games.name: Rocky

games.description: Roller Disco is a solid-state widebody table similar in size to the "Genie" model, features vibrant and colorful artwork that captures the essence of the disco era.
games.name: Roller Disco

games.description:
The RollerCoaster Tycoon pinball machine, released by Stern in August 2002, is a vibrant, family-friendly game designed by Pat Lawlor. Based on the popular PC game, it features a playfield adorned with four roller coaster-themed ramps: The Flying Ghost, The Flying Turns, The Chicago Loop, and The Rocket. These ramps are complemented by attractions like Scrambled Eggs, Bumper Cars, and the humorous Dunk the Dummy side attraction. 
The gameplay revolves around activating rides by shooting the ball to light up their status indicators from red to green. Multiball mode is triggered by locking balls through the Chicago Loop, with jackpots awarded by hitting lit rides during multiball. Completing all food stalls grants an extra ball.
games.name: RollerCoaster Tycoon

games.description: Rollergames is a pinball machine based on the short-lived TV show of the same name. This game has very addictive background music, with separate tunes for the standard game, 2 ball lock, multi-ball, "go for the wall", and jackpot mode.
games.name: Rollergames

games.description: The Rolling Stones features music from the iconic band and combines classic pinball elements with a modern twist. It includes two flippers, two ramps, and a four-ball multiball mode.
games.name: Rolling Stones, The

games.description: The Rolling Stones features music from the iconic band and combines classic pinball elements with a modern twist. It includes two flippers, two ramps, and a four-ball multiball mode.
games.name: Rolling Stones, The

games.description: Roman Victory is a 4 players solid-state pinball machine featuring Roman History theme. The table's playfield is the same as Recel's Fair Fight.
games.name: Roman Victory

games.description: Royal Flush machine features a playing card theme with multiple drop targets and a straightforward yet engaging playfield layout. The 2-player version of this game is Gottlieb's 1976 'Card Whiz'. Later remade as Gottlieb's 1983 'Royal Flush Deluxe'.nnnnMaximum displayed point score is 99,990 points per player.
games.name: Royal Flush

games.description: Royal Flush Deluxe is a solid-state pinball machine featuring a card game theme, the machine includes two flippers, no ramps, and no multiball. It uses the Gottlieb System 80A hardware and has a digital display. This is a remake of the EM version Gottlieb's 1976 'Royal Flush'.
games.name: Royal Flush Deluxe

games.description: Royal Guard and Palace Guard are electro-mechanical pinball machines. Royal Guard is the replay version, while Palace Guard is the add-a-ball variant.nnnnMaximum displayed point score is 9,999 points.
games.name: Royal Guard

games.description: "Royal Pair" and "Top Card" are two electro-mechanical pinball machines released by Gottlieb in 1974. "Top Card," introduced in August, is a single-player game with a card and gambling theme, featuring two flippers, three pop bumpers, four slingshots, and thirteen standup targets. it had a production run of 3,100 units and is known for its straightforward gameplay. "Royal Pair," released in October as the add-a-ball version for export to Italy, shares the same design and features but focuses on awarding additional balls to extend gameplay.
games.name: Royal Pair

games.description: Safe Australia is an original table inspired by Gottlieb's 1973 High Hand. Set against an Australian wildlife backdrop, the game features a looping waterfall that hides random surprises, such as spiders, snakes, sharks, or an octopus, which appear on the DMD or backglass. Short and playful, it combines classic EM-style gameplay with quirky visuals and unexpected jump-scare animations.
games.name: Safe Australia

games.description: Safe Cracker has a playfield which is noticeably narrower and shorter than a standard pinball machine. The backbox has doors that swing open to simulate a bank safe, revealing the backglass. The backglass image and lights combine to provide an interactive board game where the player acts like a bank robber. The backbox has a token launcher, dispensing any of twenty different tokens when certain goals are achieved. Time-based game.
games.name: Safe Cracker

games.description: Saloon is a Wild West-themed pinball machine that plunges players into the heart of a dusty frontier town. With bandits on the run, duels at high noon, and saloon doors swinging, players must rack up points by hitting whiskey barrels, cracking safes, and outshooting outlaws. Fast-paced gameplay, classic western sound effects, and vintage artwork make Saloon a nostalgic trip through the golden age of pinball with a Brazilian twist.
games.name: Saloon

games.description: Samba captures the festive carnival energy with bright art, vibrant sounds, and lively gameplay. Players aim for high-scoring sequences through bumpers, targets, and rollovers, with a rhythmic flow that evokes the spirit of a samba celebration. A fun, upbeat table perfect for a quick, joyful pinball session.
games.name: Samba

games.description: San Francisco is a two-player electro-mechanical pinball machine. The game features a vibrant San Francisco theme, capturing the essence of the city's landmarks and culture. The playfield includes two flippers, three jet bumpers, six passive bumpers, two slingshots, six rollover buttons, two standup targets, two kick-out holes, a gobble hole, and a rollunder. Maximum displayed point score is 1,999 points per player.
games.name: San Francisco

games.description: Original table, designed in 2022. It is based on "Mephisto" from Unidesa in 1987. This is a tribute to San Ku Kai (Message from Space: Galactic Wars), a Japanese TV series from July 8, 1978 to January 27, 1979, with a total of 27 episodes. It is a spin-off of the 1978 film Message from Space.
games.name: San Ku Kai

games.description: Sands of the Aton is a digital pinball adventure set in the heart of a mystical desert. Unearth ancient secrets as you navigate shifting quicksand, dodge traps, and face the guardians of the temple. With fast-paced multiball modes, magnetic hazards, and a rich retro soundtrack, this original VPX table blends classic 90s pinball vibes with modern gameplay twists.
games.name: Sands of the Aton

games.description:
"Pat Hand" and "Satin Doll" are two related electro-mechanical pinball machines released by Williams Electronic Games, Inc. in 1975. "Pat Hand" is a four-player machine that features three flippers, two pop bumpers, and multiple rollovers and targets. It had a production run of 6,500 units, making it a popular game of its time.

"Satin Doll" is the two-player version of "Pat Hand," sharing a similar playfield design but with four flippers and a slightly different scoring setup.
games.name: Satin Doll

games.description: Saucerer is a mod of the classic 1985 Williams machine Sorcerer. It features redesigned artwork and a new playfield layout, including moving bumpers and lanes, plus a third flipper to enhance gameplay. Fast-paced and visually dynamic, it modernizes the original with updated lighting, responsive physics, and polished visuals—delivering both nostalgia and fresh pinball action.
games.name: Saucerer

games.description: Original table, designed in 2022. It is based on "Time Fantasy" from Williams in 1983. This game is a tribute to SAW, a horror media franchise created by Australian filmmakers James Wan and Leigh Whannell, which began with the eponymous 2004 film and quickly became a worldwide pop culture phenomenon. The franchise has expanded from films into other media, including a television series, video games, comic books, music, theme park attractions, and merchandising including toys, masks, and clothing. Saw is one of the highest-grossing horror film franchises of all-time.
games.name: SAW 2022

games.description:
Scared Stiff is the sequel to the classic 1989 game, Elvira and the Party Monsters. The gameplay is simple and easy to understand, but can be hard to master - it can feel like a real achievement to make it to the end game.
What makes this game different from the first one is the quality of callouts by Cassandra Peterson, and the amount of humor in the design. Some of the humor is sexist when viewed critically and may not age well, but it fits with the character and the era.
games.name: Scared Stiff

games.description: "Schuss" is an electro-mechanical pinball machine. Designed for a single player, it features four flippers, three pop bumpers, two slingshots, four standup targets, and eleven star rollovers. At game over, instead of a number match feature, a replay is awarded on a random basis, and the word "Chance" lights up on the backglass when this happens.
games.name: Schuss

games.description: The Scooby Gang still needs your help to solve mysteries and capture villains. Listen for clues from the gang as they tell you what to do. Some clues are hidden and some are in plain sight, so... Pay attention when a clue is given. It's now on you to find the clues and learn the game. Some things are obvious and some not.
games.name: Scooby Doo

games.description: The Scorpion pinball machine, manufactured by Williams in 1980, is a wide-body solid-state game designed by Barry Oursler with artwork by Constantino Mitchell and Tony Ramunni. Notably, it was the first pinball machine to feature a multiball timer, a significant innovation at the time. The game is set in a nautical adventure theme, featuring vibrant, colorful artwork. It includes four flippers (two being used in a mini-playfield), pop bumpers, drop targets, standup targets, kick-out holes, and dual inlanes. The multiball mode is initiated by locking two balls in separate kick-out holes, and the timer counts down the duration of multiball play, rewarding players with points based on time and performance. With only 2,000 units produced, Scorpion is considered a rare and collectible machine among pinball enthusiasts.
games.name: Scorpion

games.description: Scramble pinball machine, produced by Italian manufacturer Tecnoplay in March 1987, is a solid-state, four-player game with a motocross racing theme. The playfield features two flippers, two pop bumpers, four slingshots, and four ramps.
games.name: Scramble

games.description: Scuba is a two-player electro-mechanical pinball machine. The game features a captivating underwater theme, incorporating elements of mermaids, scuba diving, and ocean mythology.nnnnMaximum displayed point score is 9,999 points per player.
games.name: Scuba

games.description: Sea Ray and Mariner, both are closely related pinball machines that share the same gameplay mechanics but differ in their player capacity. Mariner is the four-player version, while Sea Ray supports two players, both machines feature a water sports and spear-fishing theme.
games.name: Sea Ray

games.description: Beware the Sorcery of Seawitch! Before an ominous storm-tossed shoreline, two Seawitches engage in a no-holds-barred battle for supremacy while a school of mermaids watch from the sidelines. Launch the ball to loop around the upper playfield and down to the flippers, then sweep the three banks of drop targets to advance the bonus and increase the multiplier. Against the sounds of crashing waves, raise the value of the spinner, then use the two upper flippers to fling the ball around the Rip Tide and quickly build up your score.
games.name: Seawitch

games.description: Secret Agent is a fast-paced, cartoon-style spy-themed pinball table full of action and personality. Players step into the shoes of a secret agent, battling colorful villains across dynamic missions. With stackable multiballs, varied modes, vibrant visuals, and energetic voiceovers, it delivers a thrilling and playful pinball experience inspired by classic animated spy adventures.
games.name: Secret Agent

games.description:
The player is Agent 001 of the United States Secret Service, with one simple mission — protect Washington, D.C. from the evil Soviets who are targeting the nation's leaders. Patrol the streets of D.C. in your service-issued Ferrari, gun down enemy agents in front of the Capitol Building, then curve around the Beltway and lock your ball in the White House. Infiltrate the Soviet spy headquarters via the underground passage, then start a three-ball multiball for a chance at the Special.

Secret Service is memorable for its post-game karaoke mode; after each game, the table would play the chorus from "Nobody Does It Better", while displaying the lyrics on the alphanumeric score display. It also featured a Digital Stereo soundsystem, a point played up in advertisements.
games.name: Secret Service

games.description: A digital recreation of the unreleased Culik Pinball “Senna” prototype from 2020, this table captures the physical prototype's design and feel with remarkable fidelity. It supports multiple display modes (desktop, full-screen, VR, and mixed reality) and includes a customizable VR environment, allowing players to switch room styles and even enable ambient effects via in-game settings. The result is an immersive simulation that faithfully evokes the look and play of the original Senna prototype.
games.name: Senna

games.description: Original table, designed by jpsalas in 2017. It is based on the story and characters from Croteam's game "Serious Sam: The Second Encounter".
games.name: Serious Sam Pinball

games.description:
The theme is around the old Egypt Gods, and it takes place inside one temple where some of the Gods have gathered.
You, Sam, have to defeat them all.
games.name: Serious Sam Pinball II

games.description: Original table, designed in 2023. It is based on "Playboy" from Bally in 1978. This is a tribute to Sesame Street, an American educational children's television series that combines live-action, sketch comedy, animation, and puppetry.
games.name: Sesame Street

games.description: Shamrock is a playing card-themed pinball machine. The game was produced in two versions: a single-player electro-mechanical (EM) version and a four-player EM version. Both versions feature two flippers, two pop bumpers, two slingshots, five standup targets, four captive balls, and four kick-out holes.
games.name: Shamrock

games.description: Step into a mystical paradise with Shangri-La, a classic electromechanical pinball machine by Williams. Featuring vibrant artwork and smooth gameplay, this machine challenges players to hit a central swinging target and rack up points through skillful nudging and precise shots. With its tropical theme and engaging layout, Shangri-La offers a nostalgic journey to an exotic land of fun and adventure.
games.name: Shangri-La

games.description: Sharkey's Shootout is a Pinball Table released by Stern Pinball in 2000. Designed by John Borg with art by veteran pinball artist John Youssi, this is a game with an unconventionally tumultuous origin. Sharkey's is about an exclusive, invitation-only pool tournament in Sharkey's Pool Hall, where a motley cast of characters — including Sharkey himself, Tex the cowboy, and a space alien — attempt to dethrone the current champion, Real Life pool expert Jeanette "The Black Widow" Lee. The player must first defeat five other players at 8-ball or 9-ball, then take on The Black Widow herself to win the generous cash prize. And the challenge extends beyond the playfield, as Sharkey's is Stern's first tournament pinball, allowing players worldwide to compete with each other.
games.name: Sharkey's Shootout

games.description: Sharp Shooter II is a solid-state electronic game with a Western cowboy theme, this machine features a 4-player setup and a variety of interesting mechanics, such as two flippers, four bumpers, seven drop targets, and a spinning target.
games.name: Sharp Shooter II

games.description: Step into the Wild West with Sharpshooter, Game Plan's best-selling pinball machine with 4,200 units sold. Fast-paced and skill-based, it challenges players to knock down drop targets, capture outlaws, and rack up bonuses. A true classic of precision and strategy.
games.name: Sharpshooter

games.description:
Sheriff from September 1971 was the first Gottlieb-machine to use a "Dummy-Zero" and the first multiplayer with a large drop-target-bank, which soon became some kind of Gottlieb-trademark. It was a very popular game in Europe. Other versions were also released. Gottlieb's 1971 'Lawman', a 2-player version single-player; Gottlieb's 1972 'Texas Ranger', a single-player Italian version and Maresa's 1972 'Dakota', a single-player Spanish version.
A count-off bonus scores after each ball played and a double-count bonus scores after the last ball. Hitting all 10 Drop Targets scores a Special. 6 Rollovers score full bonus when lit. 3 Targets open and close ball-back gate for last minute added play.
games.name: Sheriff

games.description: An unofficial copy of Gottlieb's iconic Big Indian (1974), Cherokee mirrors its Native American theme and drop-target layout. Though produced in very small numbers, this European machine offers fast, straightforward gameplay typical of late '70s pinball.
games.name: Sherokee

games.description: Ship Ahoy pinball machine features a nautical and pirate theme, and is known for its "add-a-ball" feature, allowing players to extend gameplay by earning extra balls through specific achievements on the playfield.nnnnThe replay version of this game is Gottlieb's 1976 'Buccaneer'. The Add-a-ball version for export to Italy is Gottlieb's 1976 'High Seas'.
games.name: Ship Ahoy

games.description: Ship-Mates is a four-player, electro-mechanical game with a nautical theme. It features two flippers, four pop bumpers, two slingshots, six standup targets, two kick-out holes, a rollunder, and a roto-target numbered 1, 2, and 3. Hitting all three numbers on the roto-target awards the same-player-shoots-again feature.nnnnMaximum displayed point score is 1,999 points per player.
games.name: Ship-Mates

games.description: Shooting the Rapids is a solid-state pinball machine with a Native American and canoeing theme. The game features two flippers, three pop bumpers, three slingshots, an eight-bank drop target, a spinning target, and a kicker.
games.name: Shooting The Rapids

games.description: A faithful, original 2024 table inspired by the two-film saga featuring the sentient robot Johnny 5. Players step into the shoes of an Input‑Inc. executive, aiming to boost corporate bonuses, manufacture and sell robots, outmaneuver rival Nova Robotics, and gather data—all reflected in the playfield's modes and objectives. The tables Include Two Languages, English and Spanish.
games.name: Short Circuit

games.description: Original table, designed in 2017. It is based on Shovel Knight, the retro-styled platform game released in 2014 by Yacht Club Games.
games.name: Shovel Knight

games.description: Based on the popular animated film series, Shrek brings the whimsical world of Far Far Away to life with vibrant artwork, character voices, and family-friendly gameplay. It features toys like Donkey and Dragon, along with multiball modes and film-themed missions. Mechanically, the game is a direct copy of Family Guy (2007), with re-themed artwork, sounds, and animations.
games.name: Shrek

games.description: Shuffle Inn is a shuffle-alley bowling game with a barroom theme, featuring realistic sound effects, animated scoring, and multiple game modes. With its classic woodgrain cabinet and casual vibe, it captures the feel of bar-style shuffle bowling, offering fun and competitive gameplay for up to six players.
games.name: Shuffle Inn

games.description: Original table, designed in 2016. It is based on the movie 'Silent Night, Deadly Night', a 1984 American slasher directed by Charles E. Sellier Jr., Silent Night, Deadly Night follows Billy Chapman, a traumatized orphan who, after years of abuse and a violent past, suffers a breakdown at Christmas and becomes a killer in a Santa suit.
games.name: Silent Night Deadly Night

games.description:
A Pinball about silver pinballs. In the annals of pinball, Silverball Mania stands out for its mesmerizing art; the mirrored backglass is a stunning combination of black and silver, an eye-catching attraction in any sort of light. The playfield itself depicts an abstract mercurial landscape of chrome, where muscular men and lithe women spring forth from a gigantic silver ball under the watchful tutelage of a silver wizard. Hit the various targets and spell SILVERBALL MANIA; loop the central horseshoe to raise the Disappearing Kicker, then let it kick drained balls back onto the table and try for the Carry-Over Special.
Each Silverball Mania letter is worth 1000 points, up to 44000 bonus points, times the multiplier, may be collected by these letters. Completing the sequence the first time lights the Wizard Bonus. The Supreme Wizard Bonus, worth 30000 points, lights with the second and the third completion, awards a special and lights a letter in the backglass carryover feature.
games.name: Silverball Mania

games.description: The Simpsons Pinball Party is certainly an improvement over the first Simpsons themed table released in 1990 by Data East. Gameplay is somewhat unique with a non-fan layout and a few tricky upper playfield shots. If you're a fan of The Simpsons, and a fan of pinball, this is the game for you!
games.name: Simpsons Pinball Party, The

games.description: Sing Along and Melody, both released by Gottlieb in 1967, are nearly identical electro-mechanical pinball machines. Sing Along is the replay version, while Melody is the add-a-ball variant. Both games feature a lively music theme, with Melody incorporating caroling motifs.nnnnMaximum displayed point score is 9,999 points.
games.name: Sing Along

games.description: Embark on a knightly quest with Sir Lancelot, Peyper's 1994 pinball adventure. Battle dragons, rescue the princess, and defend Camelot in a medieval world of chivalry, magic, and high-score challenges. Will you rise as the true champion of the round table?
games.name: Sir Lancelot

games.description: Bally's Six Million Dollar Man is themed upon the American science fiction television series of the same name, which ran on the ABC network for five seasons between 1973 and 1978. The show's eponymous character, the “Bionic Man” Col. Steve Austin, is featured prominently on the backglass. The game can accommodate up to six-players at a time—the first solid state game to do so. The game features two (ever-popular) Bally spinners, a bank of drop targets, a pop-up “Play-More” post, an outlane diverter gate, a kick-out hole and a 50,000 point bonus collected through stand-up targets and rollovers. The Dave Christensen art package features some of the common themes found within his oeuvre: eagles, lightning bolts and muscular bodies set amongst a red, white and blue patriotic motif.
games.name: Six Million Dollar Man, The

games.description: Hit the ramps and ride the wave in Skateball, Bally's fast-paced 1980 pinball classic. Mix skateboarding and surfing in a high-energy showdown packed with tricky shots, wild combos, and non-stop action. Can you master the ultimate skatepark challenge?
games.name: Skateball

games.description: Cruise into the arcade spirit of the '80s with Skateboard by Inder. Dodge obstacles, rack up points, and show off your skills in this retro pinball ride where style, speed, and precision rule the game. Are you ready to roll?
games.name: Skateboard

games.description: Soar into action with Sky Jump, Gottlieb's 1974 electro-mechanical classic. Perform daring jumps, hit precision targets, and chase sky-high scores in this gravity-defying pinball adventure. The Add-a-ball version of this game is Free Fall, while the Italian export version was released as Sky Dive.
games.name: Sky Jump

games.description: Sky Kings features an aviation theme, with vibrant backglass artwork depicting airplanes soaring through the skies. It's an electro-mechanical pinball machine, which was typical of the era, offering players a classic gameplay experience with features such as bumpers, slingshots, and a variety of targets.
games.name: Sky Kings

games.description: Skyrocket is a fireworks-themed pinball machine bursting with fast-paced action. Players aim for explosive target banks and skill shots to light up bonus lanes and trigger multiball. With vibrant visuals, pop bumpers, and quick loop shots, the game builds momentum like a grand finale—timing and precision lead to a dazzling high score.
games.name: Skyrocket

games.description: Skyway takes players on a high-speed ride above the city skyline. Navigate lanes, hit precise targets, and activate bonus features as you race across elevated ramps and tight loops. With smooth flow and classic Williams mechanics, Skyway rewards skillful shots and fast reflexes in a thrilling urban adventure
games.name: Skyway

games.description: Original table, designed in 2022. It is based on "Spirit" from Gottlieb in 1982. This is a tribute to Slayer, an American thrash metal band from Huntington Park, California, formed in 1981 by guitarists Jeff Hanneman and Kerry King, drummer Dave Lombardo and bassist/vocalist Tom Araya. Slayer's fast and aggressive musical style made them one of the "big four" bands of thrash metal.
games.name: Slayer

games.description: An original 1994 electronic pinball machine from the Spanish manufacturer Sleic, playable by up to four players. It features classic elements two flippers, pop bumpers, slingshots, drop targets, spinner and captive balls—along with a dot‑matrix display and custom gameplay rules. Developed using the code of a similar 1984 Petaco table but enhanced with new animations, revised layout, and unique rule elements.
games.name: Sleic Pin-BALL

games.description: Slick Chick is a lively 1963 pinball classic with a mid-century "Playboy-inspired" theme and a fun, retro vibe. Players score by hitting rollover lanes, pop bumpers, and numbered targets. Completing sequences lights specials and extra balls, rewarding precise aim and control. With its charming artwork and smooth gameplay, Slick Chick delivers timeless vintage entertainment.
games.name: Slick Chick

games.description: Smart Set is an electro-mechanical pinball machine themed around boating and leisure. Players shoot for pop bumpers, rollovers, and numbered targets to light specials and earn replays. With smooth gameplay and laid-back 1960s artwork, it captures the spirit of carefree recreation on the water.
games.name: Smart Set

games.description: Original Electro-mechanical table, designed in 2015. It is based on "Big Shot" from Gottlieb in 1974. Smurfette (French: La Schtroumpfette) is the main protagonist from the comic strip The Smurfs.
games.name: Smurfette

games.description: Snow Derby and Snow Queen are two pinball machines released by Gottlieb in 1970. Both machines share the same gameplay design but differ in the number of players—Snow Queen accommodates four players, while Snow Derby is for two players, these machines feature a winter sports theme with skiing and snowmobiles.
games.name: Snow Derby

games.description: Snow Queen and Snow Derby are two pinball machines released by Gottlieb in 1970. Both machines share the same gameplay design but differ in the number of players—Snow Queen accommodates four players, while Snow Derby is for two players, these machines feature a winter sports theme with skiing and snowmobiles.
games.name: Snow Queen

games.description: Soccer is a 2-player electro-mechanical pinball machine with a fast-paced football theme. Players aim for goals by hitting spinners, targets, and bumpers to rack up points. The 4-player version of this game is Gottlieb's 1975 Super Soccer. The same cabinet artwork, though in different colors, also appears on Gottlieb's 1977 Team One and Kicker.
games.name: Soccer (Gottlieb)

games.description: Soccer is a electro-mechanical pinball machine. players kick off by choosing a team color and score goals by hitting pop bumpers and the upper center kick-out hole. A unique backbox animation shows a soccer ball being "kicked" into a bell when a goal is made. With two flippers, four pop bumpers, slingshots, and multiple targets, it delivers fast-paced gameplay that captures the spirit of soccer. Around 2,850 units were produced.
games.name: Soccer (Williams)

games.description: Soccer Kings featuring a soccer theme and solid-state electronics. Known for its unique gameplay, the machine includes two playfields—one main and one upper "attack zone" and uses five flippers, four on the main playfield and one in the attack zone.
games.name: Soccer Kings

games.description: Solar City is a 2-player electro-mechanical pinball machine by Gottlieb featuring a classic drop-target layout. It shares its playfield design with several other titles, including El Dorado, Gold Strike, Target Alpha, and Canada Dry. The game offers fast-paced action with strategic target shots and classic 1970s gameplay.
games.name: Solar City

games.description: Solar Fire featuring a space-themed design with four flippers, two ramps, and a three-ball multiball mode. Part of the Williams System 7 series, it has a production run of 782 units.
games.name: Solar Fire

games.description: Solar Ride is a faithful EM clone of Gottlieb's 1979 classic and preserves the original's space-themed playfield, featuring three flippers, three pop bumpers, star rollovers, two kick-out holes, a 5-bank drop-target bank, and bonus saucers. With mechanical scoring displays and enhanced visuals, it delivers an authentic retro gaming experience with modern polish.
games.name: Solar Ride (Eletromatic)

games.description: Solar Ride features a captivating outer space theme. This machine was produced in two versions: an electro-mechanical model and a solid-state version.
games.name: Solar Ride (Gottlieb)

games.description: Solar Ride by Rowamet is a faithful 1982 clone of Gottlieb's 1979 electro-mechanical table. It preserves the original's space-themed layout and includes digital scoring displays, three flippers, bumpers, drop targets, and bonus saucers. The mod enhances visuals and lighting while retaining authentic EM gameplay, offering a nostalgic, high-quality digital experience.
games.name: Solar Ride (Rowanet)

games.description: Solar Wars is a sci-fi themed pinball machine by Sonic, set in a futuristic space battle. Players must navigate cosmic hazards and defeat alien invaders to restore peace to the galaxy. Fast-paced gameplay and vibrant artwork make it a standout from the early '80s arcade scene.
games.name: Solar Wars

games.description: Solids N Stripes is a billiards-themed pinball machine by Williams. Inspired by classic pool hall action, players aim to sink solid and striped balls by hitting specific targets and completing skill shots. Its vibrant design and smooth gameplay capture the spirit of competitive cue sports.
games.name: Solids N Stripes

games.description: Solitaire is the Italian add-a-ball version of Gottlieb's 1967 Diamond Jack, which itself is the add-a-ball counterpart to the U.S. King of Diamonds replay model. It was the first machine from this manufacturer to feature a score reel for the thousands digit, allowing for higher scoring. Previous models used a silkscreened '1' in this position. In Italy, operators often modified these machines by installing longer 3" flippers and replacing the original pop bumpers with updated versions from the 1970s.
games.name: Solitaire

games.description: Original table, designed in 2020 and inspired by the game "Sonic the Hedgehog Spinball", also known as Sonic Spinball, a 1993 pinball video game developed by Sega for the Sega Genesis.
games.name: Sonic the Hedgehog Spinball

games.description: The Sopranos pinball machine immerses players in the world of the hit HBO series. The gameplay challenges players to rise through the ranks to become the Boss, featuring various elements from the show including the dancing girls of the Bada Bing, Tony Soprano's boat "The Stugots," a talking fish, and a safe that opens when hit by the ball​.
games.name: Sopranos, The

games.description: With the Sorcerer's flashing eyes and numerous taunts, it became the second-best-selling pinball game of the year, and is fondly remembered for its straightforward but challenging gameplay, fast action, and ornate art by Pam Erickson. The table itself is the named Sorcerer, who is being challenged in a magic duel by the player. Invoke his title to build your magic power, then use it to summon demons, earn extra balls and light the special. But move quickly with the upper flipper, or else the magic will dissipate and leave you powerless. For more points, lock two balls to start multiball, then repeatedly shoot the ramp to build the multiball multiplier up to 5x.
games.name: Sorcerer

games.description: Original table, designed in 2019. It is based on "Titan" from Taito do Brasil in 1982. The table is based on the "Legacy of Kain" video game series by Crystal Dynamics, where the main character, a handsome vampire named Raziel, under the ever watching eyes of a giant squid, has to unravel his past and future, all the while dodging and dealing with his dysfunctional family!
games.name: Soul Reaver

games.description: Sound Stage features flippers, pop bumpers, slingshots, standup targets, a kick-out hole, and a unique under-playfield spinning disc triggered by specific shots. Known for its lively mechanical sounds and smooth gameplay, it's one of the last EM tables made by the company. Chicago Coin's 1976 Juke Box is the four-player version of this game, featuring different artwork.
games.name: Sound Stage

games.description: Space Cadet is a retro-futuristic pinball game where the player takes on the role of a young pilot at the Space Academy, completing missions to rise through the ranks of the space fleet. Popularized through its inclusion in Windows XP as 3D Pinball for Windows – Space Cadet, this cult classic captivated millions of players with its immersive space-themed atmosphere and dynamic gameplay mechanics.
games.name: Space Cadet

games.description: Space Cadet is a retro-futuristic pinball game where the player takes on the role of a young pilot at the Space Academy, completing missions to rise through the ranks of the space fleet. Popularized through its inclusion in Windows XP as 3D Pinball for Windows – Space Cadet, this cult classic captivated millions of players with its immersive space-themed atmosphere and dynamic gameplay mechanics.
games.name: Space Cadet

games.description: Space Cadet is a retro-futuristic pinball game where the player takes on the role of a young pilot at the Space Academy, completing missions to rise through the ranks of the space fleet. Popularized through its inclusion in Windows XP as 3D Pinball for Windows – Space Cadet, this cult classic captivated millions of players with its immersive space-themed atmosphere and dynamic gameplay mechanics.
games.name: Space Cadet

games.description: Space Gambler delivers classic late-70s pinball action with a sci-fi twist. Players aim to rack up points by hitting drop targets, spinning bumpers, and activating bonus features tied to the game's space casino theme. Strategic shots and precise timing are key to lighting up special modes, increasing multipliers, and earning extra balls. Fast, challenging, and packed with retro charm, it's a true test of skill over luck among the stars.
games.name: Space Gambler

games.description: Space Invaders is released by Bally in 1980 as a spinoff of the popular arcade game. While the gameplay was classic for the era—shooting pinballs at alien targets—Bally added depth with a promotional comic: Giger-inspired aliens, disguised in arcade cabinets, emerge to possess pinball machines and captivate human minds. The artwork, strongly influenced by Alien, led to a lawsuit from 20th Century Fox, halting production at 11,000 units before a settlement was reached.
games.name: Space Invaders

games.description: Space Invaders is released by Bally in 1980 as a spinoff of the popular arcade game. While the gameplay was classic for the era—shooting pinballs at alien targets—Bally added depth with a promotional comic: Giger-inspired aliens, disguised in arcade cabinets, emerge to possess pinball machines and captivate human minds. The artwork, strongly influenced by Alien, led to a lawsuit from 20th Century Fox, halting production at 11,000 units before a settlement was reached.
games.name: Space Invaders

games.description: Based on the hit movie, Space Jam pinball teams up Michael Jordan with the Looney Tunes in a quest to defeat the Monstars. Players relive key moments from the film through themed modes, voice clips, and animated features. Score big with slam-dunk shots, fast ramps, and chaotic multiball as you help the Tune Squad win the ultimate intergalactic basketball game.
games.name: Space Jam

games.description:
Space Mission is a 4-Player pinball machine from January 1976, manufactured by Williams Electronic Games, Inc. Designed by Steve Kordek with the art by Christian Marche, the backglass art was derived from a picture Steve Kordek obtained from NASA. The picture surely was of the painting made by noted space artist Robert McCall (1919-2010).
The 2-Player version of this game is Williams' 1976 'Space Odyssey'.
Makin A, B or C lites eject holes which, when lit, lite double bonus. When A, B or C is lit, position of swinging target lite increases spinner value and lites extra ball rollover lane at the top of the playfield. Making A, B and C lites bottom rollover lanes, alternately, for 1 Replay.
games.name: Space Mission

games.description: Space Odyssey features a sci-fi space theme inspired by Stanley Kubrick's film "2001: A Space Odyssey.", this electromechanical pinball machine includes two flippers, two pop bumpers, and various targets such as a spinning target and a swinging target. The 4-player version of this game is Williams' 1976 'Space Mission'.
games.name: Space Odyssey

games.description: Space Orbit is a electro-mechanical pinball machine with a classic outer space theme. Designed for one player, it features two flippers, four pop bumpers, and a variety of rollover and stand-up targets. With fast-paced gameplay and vibrant space-themed artwork, it offers a nostalgic journey into vintage arcade action.
games.name: Space Orbit

games.description: Space Patrol by Taito do Brasil is a rare 1980 electro-mechanical pinball machine with a sci-fi space adventure theme. Featuring two flippers, pop bumpers, and a range of classic targets, it delivers fast-paced action and colorful artwork typical of Taito's unique Brazilian style.
games.name: Space Patrol

games.description: Space Poker is a electro-mechanical pinball machine that blends a space theme with poker-inspired elements. Equipped with two flippers, pop bumpers, and card-themed targets, it offers a unique mix of fast gameplay and retro sci-fi aesthetics. A distinctive creation from Brazil's pinball scene.
games.name: Space Poker

games.description: Space Riders is a 1978 wide-body pinball machine from Atari, themed around futuristic motorcycle racing. It features bold sci-fi artwork, two flippers, pop bumpers, drop targets, spinners, and bonus multipliers. Players spell out words like “BIKE” and “CITY” to unlock rewards and chase high scores. Its distinctive sound design and retro aesthetic make it a standout from Atari's early solid-state era.
games.name: Space Riders

games.description: Space Station was designed by Barry Oursler, with artwork by Tim Elliott, sounds by Brian Schmidt, and software by Ed Boon, co-creator of Mortal Kombat. Space Station is widely considered to be an unofficial sequel to Space Shuttle. It features a second set of "STATION" spot targets that scores its own independently-cycling value and builds upon the Stop-N-Score feature. Station also features a mini upper playfield above the pop bumpers and a rotating space station toy used to direct balls towards the locks on either side of the playfield.
games.name: Space Station

games.description: Space Train is a 1987 pinball machine by MAC S.A. that takes players on a cosmic journey aboard a futuristic space locomotive. Featuring classic gameplay with a sci-fi twist, it includes flippers, bumpers, and captive balls, all set in a sleek, modular design.
games.name: Space Train

games.description: Space Walk is notable for being the last electro-mechanical (EM) game made by the company. This two-player machine shares its playfield layout with the solid-state model "Count-Down."
games.name: Space Walk

games.description:
Williams' single-player Spanish Eyes is notable for its polarizing, mosaic-style art package. It also features a pop bumper situated between the flippers and a center horseshoe lane; two design hallmarks of long-time Williams designer Norm Clark. The same characters and art style were employed for the art package of Williams' single-player Granada, which was released the same year as Spanish Eyes but featured a completely different layout. The artwork is not from Christian Marche as is widely believed, but from John Craig instead. The add-a-ball version of this game is Williams' 1972 'Granada' but with a different playfield layout.
Making letters A-B-C-D-E and making numbers 1-2-3-4-6 Score Extra Ball and lites center hoop to score extra ball. It also lites bottom rollovers to score 5000 points.
games.name: Spanish Eyes

games.description: Speakeasy and The 30's are electro-mechanical pinball machines released by Spanish manufacturer Playmatic in 1977. Speakeasy is the four-player version, while The 30's is the single-player counterpart. Both machines feature a 1930s gambling theme, complete with mechanical backbox animation that simulates slot machine reels.
games.name: Speakeasy (Playmatic)

games.description: Special Force features a military theme with two flippers, three ramps, and a three-ball multiball mode and produced 2,750 units.
games.name: Special Force

games.description: Special Force Girls is a localized German version of Bally Midway's 1986 solid-state game Special Force, featuring the same playfield but with a redesigned backglass showcasing female characters instead of the original military artwork. The four-player machine includes two flippers, three pop bumpers, a set of drop targets, and a helicopter whirlpool feature that simulates a spinning ball with accompanying rotor sounds.
games.name: Special Force Girls

games.description: Spectrum featuring a futuristic computer theme, it stands out for its strategic gameplay, requiring players to hit specific targets to unlock colors and sequences. It es nnbased on the 1970 2-player board game Mastermind.
games.name: Spectrum

games.description:
The table encompasses all three films in Sam Raimi's Spider-Man trilogy, which in turn were based on the prior comics and television series.

The goal of the table is to defeat the villains from all three movies: Green Goblin from Spider-Man, Doctor Octopus from Spider-Man 2, Sandman and Venom from Spider-Man 3. Once the player defeats all four villains, they'll have a chances to experience Battle Royale.
games.name: Spider-Man - Vault Edition

games.description:
The table encompasses all three films in Sam Raimi's Spider-Man trilogy, which in turn were based on the prior comics and television series.

The goal of the table is to defeat the villains from all three movies: Green Goblin from Spider-Man, Doctor Octopus from Spider-Man 2, Sandman and Venom from Spider-Man 3. Once the player defeats all four villains, they'll have a chances to experience Battle Royale.
games.name: Spider-Man - Vault Edition

games.description: Spin Out is a single-player electro-mechanical game features two flippers, two pop bumpers, two slingshots, and a unique roto-target mechanism. Each instance of four adjacent lit numbers awards one replay. The number "4" appears only once on the roto-target.
games.name: Spin Out

games.description: Spin Wheel is a four-player electro-mechanical pinball machine. The game features classic play elements such as two flippers, three pop bumpers, two slingshots, and five kick-out holes, along with standup targets and kickback lanes. Its standout feature is a spinning light animation in the backglass, activated during play for big scores and extra-ball chances.
games.name: Spin Wheel

games.description: Spin-A-Card and Hearts and Spades are 1969 pinball machines with identical playfields but different reward systems. Spin-A-Card focuses on replay-based gameplay, where players aim to complete card sets to earn replays, while Hearts and Spades is an add-a-ball version designed to grant extra balls upon completing similar objectives. Both machines feature two flippers, pop bumpers, kick-out holes, and spinning backglass lights.
games.name: Spin-A-Card

games.description: Spinning Wheel is an electro-mechanical pinball machine. Its central feature is a circular spinning ring of 10 lights, each color representing different point values, lighting up simultaneously on the playfield and backglass. Sinking the ball into side lanes or lower holes scores the current light's value, with a “VALUE 10 TIMES” multiplier and a special “FREE GAME” bonus available. The game also features innovative “zipper” flippers that close together to trap the ball and help players aim for high-value lanes.
games.name: Spinning Wheel

games.description: Spirit is a widebody pinball machine featuring a two-level playfield, six flippers, two ramps, and a three-ball multiball mode. The game includes a spinning backbox disc similar to that of Black Hole. While it shares similarities with Haunted House, it offers improved gameplay, likely due to the absence of a lower playfield and the inclusion of multiball features. However, it is known for reliability issues unless certain modifications are made.
games.name: Spirit

games.description: Spirit of 76 is a patriotic-themed electro-mechanical game, celebrating the American Bicentennial, it features a striking red, white, and blue color scheme. The 2-player version of this game is Gottlieb's 1976 'Pioneer'. A special 2-player Add-a-ball version, Gottlieb's 1976 'New York'
games.name: Spirit Of 76

games.description: Split Second features a carnival and amusement park theme with four flippers, one ramp, and a three-ball multiball mode, it is a wide-body game running on the Stern M-200 MPU system.
games.name: Split Second

games.description: Spot Pool showcases a billiards theme, this game is the version of Gottlieb's 1976 'Bank Shot' made for export to Italy. The replay version of this game is Gottlieb's 1976 'Sure Shot'.
games.name: Spot Pool

games.description: The Spot-A-Card is an electro-mechanical game, this game features a card and gambling theme, utilizing two flippers, three pop bumpers, four kick-out holes, and a gobble hole.
games.name: Spot-A-Card

games.description: Spy Hunter is a Pinball Spin-Off of the hit arcade racing game of the same name. Designed by Greg Kmiec with art by Tony Ramunni, it was released by Bally/Midway in 1984. In this game, the player must help Agent GK and his partner as they battle enemy agents on land, sea, and air. Make the Skill Shot to open the safety gate, then take to the air with missiles and a one-man jet to double and triple the playfield targets. Drive through the Weapons Warehouse for armament, then drop out to engage the target in a deadly battle over the drain. Knock down the drop targets to build the score towards a Special, hit the SHOT targets to light the spinner, then enter the saucer hideout and collect the Hunter bonus.
games.name: Spy Hunter

games.description: A 2025 original solid-state pinball table inspired by the hit series Netflix Squid Game. It features custom missions, vibrant theming, and immersive gameplay, complete with a dedicated VR room, it blends polished mechanics with strong visual appeal.
games.name: Squid Game

games.description: Stampede is a western-themed electro-mechanical pinball machine featuring two flippers, pop bumpers, rollover lanes, and a bonus countdown. It's known for its fast-paced gameplay and classic cowboy atmosphere. The 4-player version of this game is Stern's 1977 'Rawhide'.
games.name: Stampede

games.description:
Jump into this late-'70s Williams EM pinball classic, where every shot counts! Star Action features a central spinning turntable—hit the posts to rotate it and light up 10 surrounding lamps, unlocking Double and then Triple scoring. With wide flippers, fast drop targets, and energetic pop bumpers, the gameplay stays dynamic and addictive.
It's convertible between add-a-ball and novelty play, offering flexibility for different locations. The replay version of this game is Triple Action.
games.name: Star Action

games.description: Star Fire is a space-themed electro-mechanical pinball machine by Playmatic, featuring two flippers, pop bumpers, and vibrant sci-fi artwork. It delivers classic gameplay with a retro-futuristic vibe.
games.name: Star Fire

games.description: Star Gazer is known for its celestial theme and unique gameplay elements, it features a striking fantasy and space-themed art style by Gerry Simkus.
games.name: Star Gazer

games.description: Star God is a sci-fi themed solid-state pinball machine by Zaccaria, featuring two flippers, drop targets, pop bumpers, and colorful futuristic artwork. It's known for its fast gameplay and distinctive Italian design.
games.name: Star God

games.description: Star Light is a solid-state pinball machine featuring a space theme, it includes two flippers and offers a two-ball multiball feature. Only 100 units were produced, making it a rare collectible. Compare this playfield layout to that of Williams' 1979 wide-body game, Laser Ball.
games.name: Star Light

games.description: Star Pool is an electro-mechanical pinball machine with a pool and billiards theme. Designed for up to four players, it features two flippers, pop bumpers, and various targets, including ten stand-up targets representing billiard balls. The machine is known for its engaging playfield design, which simulates aspects of pool games.
games.name: Star Pool

games.description:
Gottlieb's Race Thru Space!  Another extended wide-body machine like Circus.  Lots of fun to play, two Varitargets, a hard to hit bonus saucer, and fast loops.

Game objectives summary: Spell out S-T-A-R or R-A-C-E on the vari-targets to scoop the Special. Make the top rollover lanes to increase the multiplier bonus value of the central drop-targets. Look to make the top loop or drop the top left drop-target bank a couple of times to set up the Extra Ball chance.
games.name: Star Race

games.description: Star Ship is a sci-fi themed pinball machine that launches players into deep space with fast-paced electro-mechanical gameplay. The backglass features the iconic spaceship from the 1960s Star Trek TV series—an image later reused on Bally's 1979 Star Trek pinball. Interestingly, the playfield layout is identical to that of Bally's 1979 Supersonic, offering familiar action with a cosmic twist. A vintage classic blending pop culture and pinball history.
games.name: Star Ship

games.description: Star Trek is a solid-state pinball machine based on the original Star Trek TV series. It features two flippers, three pop bumpers, two slingshots, a four-bank drop target, five stand-up targets, and a kick-out hole.
games.name: Star Trek (Bally)

games.description: Star Trek is a solid-state pinball machine based on the original Star Trek TV series. It features two flippers, three pop bumpers, two slingshots, a four-bank drop target, five stand-up targets, and a kick-out hole.
games.name: Star Trek (Bally)

games.description:
Star Trek: The Next Generation is a pinball machine that is based on the TV show of the same name. It is a wide-body machine, which means it is larger than a standard pinball machine. Wide-body pins come with their unique characteristics, which some players enjoy, and others do not.
Although STTNG has some flaws, it is still an enjoyable machine to play. It features mode-based play that is challenging, as well as great callouts and theming. The cannons on each of the slingshots are also a lot of fun to shoot and are rather iconic for this game.
games.name: Star Trek: The Next Generation

games.description: This table is based on the original Star Trek television series, the game features two flippers, two ramps, and a three-ball multiball mode. The machine integrates thematic elements from the show, including iconic characters and sound effects.
games.name: Star Trek 25th Anniversary

games.description:
Stern Star Trek pinball machine, released in 2013, is based on the 2009 "Star Trek" film and its sequel "Star Trek Into Darkness." Designed by Steve Ritchie, this machine puts players in the role of Captain James T. Kirk, leading the crew of the USS Enterprise on various missions to protect the Federation.

Related machines: Star Trek (Premium), Star Trek (Pro), Star Trek (LE), Star Trek (Vault), Star Trek (Premium Vault), Star Trek (Enterprise Limited Edition)
games.name: Star Trek LE

games.description:
Stern Star Trek pinball machine, released in 2013, is based on the 2009 "Star Trek" film and its sequel "Star Trek Into Darkness." Designed by Steve Ritchie, this machine puts players in the role of Captain James T. Kirk, leading the crew of the USS Enterprise on various missions to protect the Federation.

Related machines: Star Trek (Premium), Star Trek (Pro), Star Trek (LE), Star Trek (Vault), Star Trek (Premium Vault), Star Trek (Enterprise Limited Edition)
games.name: Star Trek LE

games.description: Original table, designed in 2022. It is based on "Skateball" from Bally in 1980. This is a tribute to Spock, a fictional character in the Star Trek media franchise. He first appeared in the original Star Trek series serving aboard the starship USS Enterprise as science officer.
games.name: Star Trek Spock Tribute

games.description: Star Trip is a cocktail-style pinball machine with retro sci-fi flair and classic late-'70s design. It features drop targets, a spinner, bumpers, and a bonus kick-out hole. Players aim to light lanes, complete target banks, and build bonus multipliers for high scores. It shares the same playfield layout as Game Plan's 1979 Family Fun!—bringing a familiar layout into a cosmic setting. Compact, energetic, and full of vintage charm.
games.name: Star Trip

games.description: Join the Rebel Alliance for death defying action in your quest to destroy the Empire's ultimate weapon, the evil Death Star. Make the universe safe again while collecting tri-ball and double jackpots as you and Luke Skywalker save the day.
games.name: Star Wars (Data East)

games.description: Join the Rebel Alliance for death defying action in your quest to destroy the Empire's ultimate weapon, the evil Death Star. Make the universe safe again while collecting tri-ball and double jackpots as you and Luke Skywalker save the day.
games.name: Star Wars (Data East)

games.description: Join the Rebel Alliance for death defying action in your quest to destroy the Empire's ultimate weapon, the evil Death Star. Make the universe safe again while collecting tri-ball and double jackpots as you and Luke Skywalker save the day.
games.name: Star Wars (Data East)

games.description: Original table, designed in 2022. It is based on Gamatron from Pinstar in 1985.
